summary: The group answers, with a machine-checked witness, the k = 10 case of an open question that Grünbaum published in the Mathematical Intelligencer (2010). The informal account adds a classification by exact computation of the face-to-face lattice tilers of class C(6) that are unions of golden rhombohedra. The audience is specialists in discrete geometry: tilings, parallelohedra, zonohedra and rhombic polyhedra. The literature account is careful. The quotations of Grünbaum's question and of his remarks on indentation match his author's version. The submission discloses Inchbald's earlier dimpled triacontahedron, an unproved web example of the same family, and does not claim priority. It states plainly that Senechal–Taylor (2023) was not read and that its statement about that paper rests on private correspondence. No omitted prior result was found that would change the public account.

internal_notes.message: Checked against the source: the open question, the known cases k = 4, 6, 8 (cube; Kepler and Bilinski dodecahedra; D1, D2), 'No information is available for any k ≥ 10', the eightfold indentation of T cited to Williams p. 196, the remark 'None of the other isozonohedra obtainable by indentation of F or T seem to be parallelohedra', and spherical type (surface homeomorphic to a sphere, adjacent faces not coplanar). All are quoted accurately. The question is genuine, published and specific, so a credible specialist audience in discrete geometry and tilings (parallelohedra, zonohedra, rhombic polyhedra, quasicrystal-related golden rhombohedra) is affirmatively identified.

Confirmed that the page describes a rhombic triacontahedron with four face triplets dimpled in tetrahedral alternation ('an oblate hexahedron scooped out') as 'a conventional spacefiller' with 'cubic periodicity'. It gives no proof, no lattice and no mention of zones or Grünbaum. This matches the submission's description. The submission's handling is honest: it calls this an earlier k = 10 example and makes no first-example claim. The Internet Archive dates (absent 31 Mar 2022, present 23 Mar 2023) were not independently checked. A Sketchfab model by another author ('Dimpled Rhombic Triacontahedron') also appears in search results; this is further web presence of the same solid and does not change the account.

Inchbald's informal example (2023) reduces the novelty of mere existence at k = 10, but novelty is not required. What is contributed is a complete verified proof of every property Grünbaum's question asks for (spherical type, monohedral golden rhombi, all zones of 10, face-to-face lattice tiling), together with a structural classification of class C(6) and its k = 8 analogue that explains D1, D2, GET A, GET B and Inchbald's solid. This is plausibly worth a research note in discrete geometry, for example in Geombinatorics, Discrete Comput. Geom., Math. Intelligencer or Acta Cryst. A. The classification is not formalized; it is disclosed as exact computation outside Lean with its scope stated (only C(6), only face-to-face lattice tilings, only unions of golden rhombohedra, five surfaces undecided). Notability is not at the 5 anchor: interest is mostly confined to specialists, and the existential question at k = 10 already had an informal example.

Closed access; the reviewer saw only the abstract ('three new nonconvex parallelohedra ... a counterexample to a statement by Grünbaum'). Which statement of Grünbaum's is refuted could not be determined. One candidate is the indentation remark ('none ... seem to be parallelohedra'), which GET A/B and Inchbald's solid would also contradict. The abstract says their solids derive from skewed skeletons of Fedorov's parallelohedra, starting from a truncated octahedron, which suggests they are not golden rhombic monohedra with zones of 10, but this is not confirmed. The submission discloses precisely that the paper was not read and that the non-identity claim rests on unverifiable correspondence, and it claims no priority from it. This is a tooling and access limitation, not a finding.

Not cited by the submission. It contains a family P_n of sphere-like rhombic monohedral parallelohedra with no coplanar faces, and notes that multiple indentations of T 'have not been examined in detail'. Grünbaum's later 2010 statement 'no information ... k ≥ 10' implies P_n has no uniform zones of size 10 or more, so this omission does not change the public account. Adding it would be a minor bibliographic improvement.

internal_notes.evidence: Grünbaum indentation remark vs. the classification
internal_notes.message: The submission quotes Grünbaum's remark that no other indentations of T seem to be parallelohedra but does not say outright that GET A, GET B and Inchbald's solid contradict it. A sentence saying so would sharpen the account. This is not a material omission, because the facts are all present.

The submission says Mathlib has ZSpan fundamental domains but no parallelohedra or polyhedron zones, and that no systematic search of other proof libraries was made. No conflicting formalization was found or is plausible. This is a minor limitation.

These standard background attributions are correct: convex parallelohedra have belts of 4 or 6 only, so any example with k ≥ 8 is nonconvex; and the golden rhombohedra are the cells of the 3D Penrose (Ammann–Kramer) tiling. Williams, Natural Structure p. 196 is disclosed as not read; the reviewer did not check it either.

what_would_reach_higher: Read Senechal–Taylor (2023) in full, through an author copy, an interlibrary loan or a request to the authors, and state from the text which statement of Grünbaum's it refutes and that its three solids are not golden rhombic monohedra with every zone of 10 faces. This replaces the reliance on private correspondence with a checkable citation.

State explicitly that GET A, GET B and Inchbald's dimpled triacontahedron contradict Grünbaum's tentative remark that no other indentations of T seem to be parallelohedra, and relate this to the depth-4 search result (exactly three rank-3 solids).
Cite Grünbaum's Supplement to Bilinski (P_n family; multiple indentations of T 'not examined in detail') and say why P_n does not give uniform zones of 10 or more.

Formalize the C(6) classification in Lean, or at least the exhaustive enumeration and the three lemmas, so that the classification becomes independently checkable rather than an informal computational claim; this is the main lever toward broader interest.

Address k ≥ 12 (for example class C(7), if golden or other rhombi allow it), or prove a non-existence result in a broader class. Settling the general-k question would move the result beyond the narrow k = 10 case.

Archive the Inchbald page versions with stable Internet Archive URLs in the references, and read Williams, Natural Structure p. 196 (Grünbaum's eightfold indentation of T) to confirm it is not a k = 10 example.

Run and record a systematic search of other proof libraries (Archive of Formal Proofs, Coq/Rocq, Isabelle, HOL Light) and of OEIS-style or Polyhedra databases for formalized parallelohedra or zone results.
